messages:
Aisha: FYI two concurrent docs PRs are diverging on how to present tool-calling outputs in examples. One enforces an envelope shape for all outputs, the other shows compact parsed JSON when parsing succeeds. Thoughts?
Tom B: For newcomer UX, compact parsed JSON is easier to read. But we must add a clear interop section for teams relying on the envelope.
Leah: Agreed. Proposal: tutorial examples -> compact. Advanced/compat -> envelope + explicit fallback code. Also include streaming/truncation example to explain real-world failures.
Aisha: Good. Concrete pseudo-code I want in the compatibility note: `try: parsed = parse(resp); return parsed except ParseError: return {\"tool\": name, \"raw\": resp_str}`. Use `raw` as a string in docs.
Tom B: I'll add a TS/Node snippet showing both branches and how to `JSON.parse(raw)` if needed.
Leah: I'll author the Python SDK snippet and a tiny unit test snippet: `assert parse(resp) or fallback(resp)`. Also add a monitoring example: `parse_fail_rate = failed_parses / total_calls` under "how to monitor".
Aisha: Also check docs for `compact_response` flag mentions  we renamed to `compact_mode` last week. Update examples and call out the flag rename in migration note.
docs-bot: Note: docs PR #5092 touches the same files and needs a rebase.
Tom B: I'll update the samples index to point to both snippets and the migration guide.
Leah: I'll include a truncated-stream example snippet to show partial JSON and how fallback engages. Example: `{"status":"partial","data":"{\"x\":1"}` -> fallback to envelope.
Aisha: Owners: Tom -> TS + index, Leah -> Python + migration note + tests, Aisha -> compatibility paragraph + envelope example, Olivia (docs-bot flagged) will help coordinate reviews. Target: thin PRs by EOD Friday.
Tom B: Sounds good. I'll also run search-and-replace for old anchors linking to the archived invoke page.
Leah: tagging @docs-owners in the PR for quick review.
Aisha: Thanks team  once PRs land I'll draft the release-note blurb summarizing the change and the migration steps.
